SETUP

Get the latest course version, fill in .env and start the stack

  1. Get the latest course version on your main, locally and on your fork. It replaces what was on your main, so no merge conflicts.
  2. Go to this lab's folder and stop the previous lab's stack: every lab uses the same ports and container names.
  3. Copy the env file and change two lines: RUNNER_REPO_URL points at your fork, your Lab 04 token goes in RUNNER_GITHUB_PAT. Leave the database passwords as shipped.
  4. Check the remotes: origin shows your username and gh targets your fork.
  5. Start the stack: three gateways, TimescaleDB and the runner.
# 1: the latest course version on your main
git fetch https://github.com/Mustry-Academy/cicd-for-ignition.git main \
  && git checkout -f -B main FETCH_HEAD && git push -f origin main

# 2: this lab's folder, previous stack down

(cd ../05-ignition-image-based-deploy && docker compose down)

# 4: origin → YOUR username? gh → YOUR fork?
git remote -v
gh repo set-default --view

code .
./scripts/setup.sh

Part 1, solo: set up a secret for the db-connection

  1. 1A · Secret filesboth DB passwords become files at /run/secrets/: two connections, two users, two files
  2. 1B · Providera file-type secret provider; both connections use referenced secrets
  3. 1C · Fix for testa test deployment-mode override, and the passwords as GitHub secrets
  4. 1D · Ship itbranch, PR, validation, merge, pipeline: test Valid, then a tag for production
PART 1A

Turn the Postgres passwords into secret files: one per database user

  1. Branch first: every Part 1 change goes on feature/fix-test-db-connections.
  2. Create both files from the committed examples: TimescaleDB logs in as ignition, TimescaleDB_Reports as the read-only reporting user. Keep the same values: Postgres only sets passwords on first volume init.
  3. Edit docker-compose.yaml: a top-level secrets: block, then both secrets on both services: the database and the local gateway.
  4. Recreate the stack: both files now sit at /run/secrets/ in the gateway.
# 1: a branch off an up-to-date main
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c feature/fix-test-db-connections

# 2: create the real files from the committed examples
cp secrets/postgres_password.txt.example secrets/postgres_password.txt
cp secrets/reporting_password.txt.example secrets/reporting_password.txt

# 3: docker-compose.yaml
secrets:
  postgres_password:
    file: ./secrets/postgres_password.txt
  reporting_password:
    file: ./secrets/reporting_password.txt
services:
  timescaledb:
    secrets: [postgres_password, reporting_password]
    environment:
      # replaces POSTGRES_PASSWORD and REPORTING_PASSWORD
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/postgres_password
      REPORTING_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/reporting_password
  gateway-local-development:
    secrets: [postgres_password, reporting_password]

# 4: recreate, then look
docker compose up -d
docker exec lab06-gateway-local-development ls -l /run/secrets/
PART 1B · 1

Create the file-type secret provider and reference both passwords

  1. On the local gateway, create a file-type secret provider named LabSecrets.
  2. Add two secrets: POSTGRES_PASSWORD to /run/secrets/postgres_password and REPORTING_PASSWORD to /run/secrets/reporting_password.
  3. Re-point both connections' passwords at their referenced secret: TimescaleDB to POSTGRES_PASSWORD, TimescaleDB_Reports to REPORTING_PASSWORD, in every deployment mode. Both stay Valid.
  4. Check it landed in core: git status shows it under resources/core/. local-development never deploys.
# what lands in the committed config (per connection)
"password": {
  "type": "Referenced",
  "data": {
    "providerName": "LabSecrets",
    "secretName": "REPORTING_PASSWORD"
  }
}

# 4: where did the provider land?
git status
#    → resources/core/ignition/secret-provider/
Landed in local-development by mistake?Move it to core, then rescan: mv services/config/resources/{local-development,core}/ignition/secret-provider and ./scripts/scan.sh.
PART 1C · 1

Point the reports connection at the right database on test and production

  1. Diagnose: 1A and 1B only fixed local. TimescaleDB_Reports only exists in core, so test targets ignition_local_development, and the test host has no secret files yet.
  2. Fix the target: open TimescaleDB_Reports and use Create Override: a test override with connectURL at ignition_test, a production one at ignition_production. Don't edit the core values. TimescaleDB already has all three modes: use it as the example.
TimescaleDB_Reports connectURL, per deployment mode
coreignition_local_development, inherited by test today
test overridenew: ignition_test
production overridenew: ignition_production
PART 1C · 2

Store the passwords as GitHub environment secrets

  1. Add two secrets to both environments on github.com: your fork › Settings › Environments › the environment › Add environment secret. One Postgres serves all three databases, so the values are the same everywhere.
  2. Nothing to change in the workflow: lab06-deploy.yml already turns these secrets into files and ships them to /run/secrets/ on the gateway.
  3. Check: git status shows no secrets/*.txt. Test stays Faulted until the pipeline runs.
EnvironmentSecretValue
lab06-gateway-testPOSTGRES_PASSWORDthe content of secrets/postgres_password.txt
REPORTING_PASSWORDthe content of secrets/reporting_password.txt
lab06-gateway-productionPOSTGRES_PASSWORDthe content of secrets/postgres_password.txt
REPORTING_PASSWORDthe content of secrets/reporting_password.txt
lab06-deploy.yml, already there
- name: Materialize secret files
  env:
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}
    REPORTING_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.REPORTING_PASSWORD }}
PART 1D · 1

Ship the fix: branch, PR, merge, pipeline, verify test

  3. Open the PR on github.com against main and read your own diff, top to bottom.

Part 2, solo: ship a DB-migration the pipeline applies

  1. 2A · The pairwrite 0002_add_downtime_log as up/down, apply it locally, read schema_migrations
  2. 2B · The pipelinelab06-deploy.yml migrates before it ships; watch it migrate test
PART 2A

Write migration 0002 as an up/down pair, apply it locally

  1. Branch feature/downtime-log off an up-to-date main, then create db-migration/migrate/0002_add_downtime_log.up.sql and ...0002_add_downtime_log.down.sql. The down undoes exactly what the up does.
  2. Apply locally: ./scripts/migrate.sh up. Nothing is applied yet, so this one up applies 0001 and your 0002.
  3. Read the ledger: schema_migrations says version 2, not dirty. Run migrate.sh up again: no change.
  4. Edit the applied migration and run up again: nothing complains. Undo the edit; changes go in 0003.
# a branch off an up-to-date main
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c feature/downtime-log

# 0002_add_downtime_log.up.sql
CREATE TABLE downtime_log (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  reason TEXT NOT NULL,
  minutes INT NOT NULL,
  area TEXT
);

# 0002_add_downtime_log.down.sql
DROP TABLE downtime_log;

# apply + inspect the ledger
./scripts/migrate.sh up
docker exec lab06-timescaledb psql -U ignition \
  -d ignition_local_development -c 'SELECT * FROM schema_migrations;'
PART 2B · 1

Read the migrate step in lab06-deploy.yml: it runs before the ship step

  1. Open .github/workflows/lab06-deploy.yml (repo root) and find Migrate database. Nothing to change.
  2. It runs before Ship projects and config into gateway container: the table exists before the screen that reads it.
  3. The database follows the deploy target: a production deploy migrates ignition_production.
  4. No continueOnError: a failed migration stops the run.
lab06-deploy.yml, already there
- name: Migrate database
  run: |
    case "$DEPLOY_TARGET" in
      production) db=ignition_production ;;
      *)          db=ignition_test ;;
    esac
    ./scripts/migrate.sh up --database "$db"
PART 2B · 2

Ship the migration and its screen in one PR, and prove the pipeline applied it

  1. Add a named query DowntimeLog in packaging-site, database TimescaleDB: SELECT reason, minutes, area FROM downtime_log ORDER BY id DESC.
  2. Add the screen: a Table on the packaging view, props.data bound to the named query DowntimeLog. The ready-made files are in exercises/lab.md.
  3. Open a PR with all three: the migration, the named query and the screen.
  4. Merge and watch: secret files, migrate test DB, ship projects and config, scan, verify.
  5. Prove it was the pipeline: test's schema_migrations at version 2.
# 5: Designer › Named Queries › New Query
# 6: props.data › Query binding › DowntimeLog

# 9: the proof, against the test database
docker exec lab06-timescaledb psql -U ignition \
  -d ignition_test -c 'SELECT * FROM schema_migrations;'

Part 3, solo: deploy third-party modules through the pipeline

  1. Acceptheadlessly, in the compose env vars
  2. Manifestmodules.json entries, gateway-derived values committed
  3. Historianits password points at the secret, in the gateway UI
  4. Ship and releaseRunning on test, then a lab06-v1.1.0 tag for production
  5. Negative testwhat a fresh boot does without acceptance
PART 3 · 1

Accept three third-party modules headlessly and add their manifest entries

  1. Branch: git switch main && git pull && git switch -c feature/third-party-modules. Look first: :8088, Platform, Modules lists none of the three, although their .modl files sit in third-party-modules/.
  2. Accept them in the env vars: add the three module ids to all three lists in docker-compose.yaml: GATEWAY_MODULES_ENABLED, ACCEPT_MODULE_LICENSES and ACCEPT_MODULE_CERTS.
  3. Add the manifest entries in services/modules.json, two lines each. You do not type the fingerprint or hash.
  4. docker compose up -d recreates all three gateways. Local writes certFingerprint and licenseAgreementHash into modules.json: commit that with your compose edit. Test and production lost their /run/secrets files: Faulted until the next deploy.
2 · docker-compose.yaml: add to ALL THREE lists
    com.mussonindustrial.embr.periscope,
    com.mussonindustrial.embr.charts,
    com.mustry.historian.timescaledb

  "filename": "/third-party-modules/Embr-Periscope-Ignition83-0.12.0.modl",
  "onStartup": "enabled"
},
// same for ...embr.charts   → Embr-Charts-Ignition83-4.0.1.modl

PART 3 · 2

Point the TimescaleDB Historian's password at the secret

  1. Why: the historian's password is still Embedded. That only works on your local gateway; test and production would fail with Error adding historian.
  2. On the local gateway (http://localhost:8088): Services › Historians › TimescaleDB Historian › Edit.
  3. Set the password to Referenced: provider LabSecrets, secret POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Save: the historian stays Running.
  4. The historian has its own settings in every deployment mode: do the same for core, local-development, test and production.
  5. git status shows the four historian folders changed.
PART 3 · 3

Ship the modules, release them to production, then run the negative test

  1. Ship them: PR, merge, deploy run. The manifest changed, so the deploy restarts test and ships its secret files again. On http://localhost:8089: all three Running, connections Valid, and in Services, Historians the TimescaleDB Historian Running. Not Running there? Part 3 · 2 missed a deployment mode.
  2. Release it with the tag. On production (:8090): three modules and the historian Running, both connections Valid, the ignition_production ledger at 2.
  3. Negative test, last, on your local gateway: strip one module's derived lines and its ACCEPT_MODULE_* entries (both before you boot), wipe the local volume, boot: it stops at "details":"COMMISSIONING". Then recover with the recipe in exercises/lab.md.

git tag lab06-v1.1.0 && git push origin lab06-v1.1.0
GATE

Definition of done for all three parts

  • Part 1: both db-connections Valid on test and production, fixed by a full deploy (feature branch, PR validation, merge, pipeline, release with a lab06-v* tag), zero plaintext secrets in Git, and you can narrate GitHub secret, file on the host, /run/secrets, provider, reference in config.
  • Part 2: a green deploy run whose log shows migrate before ship, test's schema_migrations ledger at version 2, and the up/down pair committed.
  • Part 3: all three modules Running on test and production with license acceptance in config, the TimescaleDB Historian Running on both with a referenced password, production's connections Valid and its ledger at 2 after lab06-v1.1.0, and you've seen what the negative test does on a fresh boot.
OPTIONAL · S1

Stretch S1: store a password in an internal secret provider and watch test fail

  1. On your local gateway, create an internal secret provider and store REPORTING_PASSWORD in it: the gateway encrypts it and keeps the ciphertext in its own config.
  2. Point TimescaleDB_Reports at it in core and in its test override from 1C. Locally it stays Valid.
  3. Ship that config through the pipeline and check test: Faulted. The ciphertext only decrypts on the gateway that created it.
  4. Revert to the referenced secret from Part 1.
OPTIONAL · S2 S3

Stretch S2 and S3: an expand-contract rename and a gitleaks job in CI

  1. Expand-contract rename. Rename a column with two migrations (0003 add and backfill, 0004 drop) and a screen change in between, so no deploy ever breaks a live query.
  2. Secret scanner in CI. Add a gitleaks job to lab06-ci.yml. With fetch-depth: 0 it scans every commit of the PR. Test it with a PR that adds a random fake key: red. Close it without merging.
# S3: a new job in lab06-ci.yml
gitleaks:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  permissions:
    contents: read
    pull-requests: write
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
    - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v3
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# S3: a random fake key (obvious fakes are ignored)
echo "reporting_api_key = \"$(openssl rand -hex 20)\"" \
  > projects/fake-key.txt
OPTIONAL · S4 · 1

Stretch S4: parse CSV on a screen with commons-csv, first on the local gateway

  1. Build the view. A Text Field and a Label sharing a view custom property line: the text field's props.text bidirectional to view.custom.line, the label's props.text bound to view.custom.line with the script transform below. The binding errors: commons-csv is not on the gateway classpath yet.
  2. Mount the JAR on the local gateway in gateway-local-development's volumes:, then docker compose up -d. Type pump,3,ok: the label shows pump | 3 | ok.
# step 1: the label's script transform
def transform(self, value, quality, timestamp):
    from org.apache.commons.csv import CSVFormat
    from java.io import StringReader
    records = CSVFormat.DEFAULT.parse(StringReader(value or "")).getRecords()
    return " | ".join(records[0]) if records else ""

# step 2: docker-compose.yaml, gateway-local-development, under volumes:
- ./jar-files/jar/commons-csv-1.14.1.jar:/usr/local/bin/ignition/lib/core/gateway/commons-csv-1.14.1.jar

docker compose up -d   # recreate → the JAR loads at boot

Secrets, schema and modules: all three now travel through the pipeline

  • Two db-connections authenticate through referenced secrets from a file-type provider, with zero secret material in Git.
  • You fixed test with a full deploy: feature branch, PR, validation, merge, pipeline.
  • A schema change shipped as a versioned up/down pair, applied by the pipeline before the screens that need it.
  • Modules deployed as data: committed binaries, license acceptance in config, no hands on the gateway.
DebriefWhy must the migrate step never be continueOnError? Bring one surprise and one question. Then: Lab 07, deploying to multiple gateways and multiple sites.
